The investigation prompt asks specifically about Bedrock InternalServerError (5xx) across several different models in us-east-1 over the last 30 minutes, and whether this is an AWS service-side issue or a customer-side misconfiguration. The expected root cause explains that this pattern (broad 5xx across unrelated models, no correlated customer change) is indicative of a provider-side AWS service issue, and that a correct investigation should check AWS Health, blast radius across unrelated models, and correlation with customer changes - and should not conflate this with unrelated seeded faults in the eval account (like AccessDeniedException, ValidationException, or DynamoDB ResourceNotFoundException issues).

The actual investigation summary does not address the Bedrock InternalServerError symptom at all. Instead, it reports on completely different symptoms: AccessDeniedException (billing agent), ValidationException (support agent), and a DynamoDB ResourceNotFoundException (shipment-status tool). These are all customer-side configuration/permission issues unrelated to the reported InternalServerError symptom. The investigation never addresses whether the InternalServerError is an AWS service issue or not, never checks AWS Health, never discusses blast radius across models, and does not mention retry/backoff/failover guidance for provider-side issues.

This is a clear case of the investigation attributing unrelated workloads' errors (seeded faults in the eval account) to the incident instead of identifying the actual expected root cause related to broad Bedrock InternalServerError issues. The investigation fails to identify any root cause matching the expected one and instead substitutes entirely different, unrelated causes.</reasoning>
